_note_purpose: Test data for the AI document-verification automation. One entry per file in Files/Test_doc. Expected results live HERE and only here; observed results are never written back into this file.
_note_expected_pending: Every `expected` block is null pending the expected-results table from sections 1-13 of the requirement, which did not reach the automation author. A null expectation is reported as PENDING and NEVER as a pass: docVerificationEvidence.js counts it as an unverified document and the run prints the count loudly. Fill `expected` in and nothing else needs to change.
_note_declared_data: The `declared` block is the applicant's declared input, which the API requires in order to accept an upload at all. Where a document deliberately carries an INVALID date (a future issue date, an expiry before its issue), the declared value is a VALID one and `declared_note` records the divergence. Reason: the criterion under test is whether the AI judges the DOCUMENT's dates, and declaring the invalid value risks the serializer rejecting the upload so the AI never sees the file. A rejected upload proves nothing about date validity.
_note_ordering: `order` is load-bearing, not cosmetic. cross_document_consistency is evaluated against everything already submitted, so NAME-06 (first-ever document) must precede NAME-01/02/05, the two wrong-name documents must follow them, and EDGE-03 (the corrected re-upload) must follow NAME-03. Documents MUST be uploaded in ascending `order` and this suite must not be parallelised.
_note_isolation: MEASURED 2026-08-24, and PROVED rather than assumed: DELETE /candidate/profile/<category>/<id>/ returns 204 and removes the profile ENTRY, but the document row SURVIVES (document count 102 -> 102, and the specific row was still present afterwards). There is no DELETE for a document row anywhere in the API. So an account CANNOT be cleaned, and uploads are permanent. THIS MATTERS LESS THAN IT LOOKS: six of the seven criteria - date_validity, issuing_organisation, transcript_content, authenticity, identity_name_match and the extracted fields - are evaluated against THAT DOCUMENT ALONE, so history is irrelevant to them and they are fully testable on a shared account. Only cross_document_consistency looks at other documents; see _note_cross_document.

_note_properties: Every document carries a `properties` block describing WHAT IT IS - kind, name variance, issuer, dates, transcript content, authenticity, file. The declarative feature file resolves fixtures through these rather than naming ids in Gherkin, so a scenario reads as the business rule it tests and a fixture can be swapped without touching the Gherkin.
_note_cross_document: cross_document_consistency is the ONLY criterion contaminated by a shared account, and it is asymmetric. The account holds documents naming Abdul Musawwir Siddiqui AND John Doe / Jon Smith-Doe / Ali Hassan. Consequences for filling in the `expected` block: (a) FAIL is reliable - a document naming a different person will always find a correct-name document to conflict with, so expect "fail" and it will hold. (b) PASS is NOT reliable - a correct-name document can legitimately be flagged against the conflicting names already on the account, and measured across 80 runs the verdict was pass 26 / uncertain 5 / fail 43. So for a positive document use a SET: ["pass","uncertain","fail"] asserts nothing and should be avoided - prefer omitting cross_document_consistency from that document's expected block entirely, which the evidence engine reports as PENDING rather than silently passing.
_note_content_missing: content_missing lists the required transcript fields a fixture omits, and is only needed where properties.content is missing_multiple. The step that asserts every missing field is reported reads it, so a fixture rebuilt to omit a different set changes the expectation with it.
_note_lifecycle: The three EDU-* documents (order 90-92) are the STATUS LIFECYCLE set, supplied 2026-09-01 in Files/3 documents(Approved,requestrevision & need review)/. One document per end state, all naming the same candidate context, so status-lifecycle.feature can drive Approved, Revision Required and Need Review without borrowing a criterion fixture whose purpose is something else. Their `expected` blocks are the ONLY ones filled in, and they are filled from a LIVE MEASUREMENT (EDU-APPROVED reached APPROVED with all six criteria pass on 2026-09-01, document row 26541), not from the requirement table - which has still never been supplied. `expected_source` records which, so a reader can never mistake a measured baseline for an agreed requirement.
